object_description: compact seven-story atrium volume with roof pergola
design_condition: Placed on the northeastern edge of the plot and kept below the surrounding height horizon, the compact volume frees generous street-facing outdoor spaces and forms a raised piazza while leaving a weaker western connection.

positive.statement: The compact volume remains below the maximum height and lies within the horizon of the surrounding campus buildings.

position.rationale: Compact, low-rise massing is visible across the plan and elevations, though surrounding campus horizon is absent.

positive.statement: The reduced footprint creates high-quality outdoor spaces framed by plane trees.

position.target: outdoor spaces framed by plane trees
position.rationale: A peripheral open-space location is estimated beside the reduced footprint; trees are not distinguishable in the sample.

positive.statement: The ground-floor uses and open-space design are well coordinated, including deliveries.

position.rationale: Ground-level operational uses are anchored near a plausible southern entrance edge, without distinguishable delivery geometry.

positive.statement: The raised piazza is ideal as a meeting point and observation post.

position.rationale: The piazza is approximated as an exterior raised zone adjacent to the lower southern building edge.

positive.statement: The open framework gives the building an institutional character, with a balanced tension between rawness and noblesse.

position.rationale: Dense open framework and repetitive structural members are clearly visible around the sampled envelope.
The structural system is anchored to the visible framework, but load paths are not directly identifiable.
